page.layout: Top centre: page number "(64)". Left column: five names (Gutturales, Labiales, Palatinas, Dentales, Linguales) with Arabic script opposite each, as a two-cell list. Below, full-width running text in one column. At the foot right: the word "SECT.".

main_text.p: Dentales & linguales solares vocantur, Reli-quæ lunares.

Difficultas est in pronunciatione ح & ع; illa est profunda aspiratio, hæc cùm difficillimæ fit pronunciationis, sæpè per (a) à noftratibꝰ effertur ; imò plerumque omittitur, & secundum vocalem adjunctam pronunciatur, ut [illegible, ~3 letters] Abda.

Kaf & Kef, eodem feré modo pronuntiantur, sed plerunque ex adjuncta vocali discriminantur, uti etiam [illegible, ~2 letters] & [illegible, ~2 letters], & [illegible, ~2 letters] & [illegible, ~2 letters]. At quatuor hæ [illegible, ~6 letters] ut (d) sine discrimine pronun-tiari solent.

page.notes: The Arabic script in the left-hand list, and the Arabic letters within the running text, are too small and blurred to read letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The reference marks (a) and (d) appear in the text, but no matching notes are printed on this page. The word "folent" is printed with a long s that resembles f; it is given as "solent". The page has no running head; the catchword "SECT." is at the foot right.
